english_lines: It's going to be born!—Look, it's going to be born.
What? Where? To whom is it going to be born?
After ten months have passed, just watch—
You and I will both know.
Fondling and rejoicing,
We too can live without want. (பெற)
(வசனம்) Say it that way.
notes: The source-visible `வசனம்` cue is retained verbatim.

english_lines: (வசனம்) Ayya,
I asked the astrologer from Moolai Street the day before yesterday.
He said that after ten months
Good times will be born for us.
With my mother here like seven-and-a-half-year Saturn,
How can good times
Ever be born?
notes: The astrological `ஏழரை நாட்டு சனியன்` image is preserved rather than generalized as mere bad luck.

english_lines: They say there is a king in the seventh house;
Your marriage and mine
Will somehow happen—
That is what the astrologer clearly told me.
It's going to be born—look, it's going to be born;
In any case, ten months—
Good times for you and me. (பெற)
notes: `ஏழாமடத்தில்` is read in its astrological context as the seventh house, without altering the verified Tamil form.

translator_notes: The comic double meaning around childbirth, ten months and the birth of `good times` is preserved.
Item-level lyric authorship remains unresolved at this booklet-evidence tier; translation does not upgrade attribution.
